title: Induced Draft Fan
model_title: Induced Draft (ID) Fan with Inlet Box & Louvre Damper

introduction.definition: An induced draft (ID) fan pulls flue gas out of a boiler or furnace through the air heater and dust collector and pushes it up the stack. It keeps the furnace slightly below atmospheric pressure (balanced draft with an FD fan). It handles hot, dusty gas, so it is robust and wear-protected.
applications: Process gas exhaust after scrubbers / bag filters
key_points: Inlet dampers or VFD for control

classification.type: Centrifugal, inlet box, louvre damper control, coupled motor

introduction.summary: An induced draft (ID) fan sits after the boiler, dust collector or scrubber and sucks the hot flue gas out of the furnace, keeping it slightly below atmospheric pressure (balanced draft). It handles hot, dusty and sometimes corrosive gas, so it is robust, heavily built and often controlled by inlet dampers, inlet vanes or a variable-speed drive.

what_to_look_for: The spinning blades throw the air outward, adding velocity and pressure.

steps.text: Flue gas comes down the duct into the inlet box.
The louvre damper modulates to control furnace draft.
The spinning blades throw the air outward, adding velocity and pressure.
The scroll housing collects the air; its widening passage slows it and turns velocity into pressure.
Bearings and the coupled motor drive the shaft.

working_principle.characteristic_curve: As centrifugal fans; system resistance rises with boiler load and dust collector ΔP. Gas density (temperature) changes pressure: p ∝ ρ.

parts.material: Carbon steel; stainless or lined for corrosive gas.

parts.function: Adds energy to the air by spinning it outward.
parts.material: Steel; wear-resistant liners for dusty gas.

parts.name: Inlet Cone (Venturi)
parts.function: Guides air smoothly into the impeller eye.

parts.name: Bearing Pedestals (Plummer Blocks, Fixed & Free)

parts.name: Flexible Coupling
parts.function: Transmits torque between motor and pump while accommodating small misalignment and allowing separation for maintenance.
parts.material: Steel or cast iron hubs; elastomer or stainless-steel disc elements.

parts.name: Coupling Guard

parts.name: Electric Motor – Frame & End Shields

parts.name: Electric Motor – Stator
parts.material: Silicon electrical steel, copper magnet wire, Class F/H insulation (typical).

parts.name: Electric Motor – Rotor & Shaft
parts.function: Converts the rotating field into shaft torque (squirrel-cage induction rotor).

parts.name: Electric Motor – Bearings (DE & NDE)
parts.function: Support the motor rotor at drive and non-drive ends.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Cooling Fan
parts.function: Draws cooling air over the finned frame.

parts.name: Electric Motor – Fan Cover
parts.function: Guards the fan and directs air along the fins.

foundation: Mount on a rigid, level foundation or grouted baseplate sized for the machine mass and dynamic loads (typically ≥3–5 × machine mass for reciprocating machines).
Check for soft foot before final bolting.
alignment: Align driver and driven shafts with a laser or dial-indicator method to the coupling maker's tolerances; re-check hot alignment where thermal growth is significant.
piping: Fit expansion joints at inlet and outlet ducts for thermal movement; insulate hot ducts.
commissioning: Check rotation direction with the coupling disconnected.
Fill lubricant to the correct level and grade.
Start unloaded where possible; record vibration, temperatures, current and pressures as a baseline.

periodic.task: Clean impeller and housing; check inlet cone gap.

lubrication: Grease or oil bath for the plummer-block bearings; motor bearings per maker.

causes: Dust build-up or erosion on blades

video_tutorials.title: Induced Draft Fan — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Induced Draft Fan.
An induced draft (ID) fan pulls flue gas out of a boiler or furnace through the air heater and dust collector and pushes it up the stack.
It keeps the furnace slightly below atmospheric pressure (balanced draft with an FD fan).
It handles hot, dusty gas, so it is robust and wear-protected.
Typical applications include utility and industrial boilers; kilns and furnaces; process gas exhaust after scrubbers / bag filters; incinerators.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Scroll (Volute) Housing with Outlet, Impeller (10 backward-curved aerofoil blades), Hub & Shaft, Inlet Cone (Venturi), Inlet Box & Flue-Gas Duct.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Induced Draft Fan works.
Flue gas comes down the duct into the inlet box.
The louvre damper modulates to control furnace draft.
The spinning blades throw the air outward, adding velocity and pressure.
The scroll housing collects the air; its widening passage slows it and turns velocity into pressure.
Bearings and the coupled motor drive the shaft.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.

video_tutorials.title: Induced Draft Fan — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Induced Draft Fan.
Check bearing temperature and vibration.
Check damper actuator response.
Clean impeller and housing; check inlet cone gap.
Check coupling alignment.
Inspect impeller for erosion/cracks; re-balance.
Replace bearings.
Watch for vibration from imbalance: rising 1× running-speed vibration. Common cause: dust build-up or erosion on blades.
Watch for bearing overheating: high bearing temperature. Common cause: lack/excess of grease, misalignment.
Watch for erosion of blades: falling performance, vibration. Common cause: fly ash.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
